{{Short description|Dominating set that dominates both a graph and its complement}}
[[File:Global dominating set.svg|thumb|Two [[complement graph|complementary]] graphs, with a minimum '''global dominating set''' colored red in each]]

In [[graph theory]], a '''global dominating set''' is a [[dominating set]] <math>S</math> of a graph <math>G</math> that is also a dominating set of the [[complement graph]] <math>\bar{G}</math>. The '''global domination number''' <math>\gamma_g(G)</math> is the minimum cardinality of a global dominating set of <math>G</math>. The concept was introduced by E. Sampathkumar in 1989.<ref name="sampathkumar1989">{{cite journal |last=Sampathkumar |first=E. |title=The global domination number of a graph |journal=Journal of Mathematical and Physical Sciences |volume=23 |issue=5 |year=1989 |pages=377–385 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265428710}}</ref>

== Definition ==

Let <math>G = (V, E)</math> be a graph with vertex set <math>V</math> and edge set <math>E</math>. A set <math>S \subseteq V</math> is a '''dominating set''' of <math>G</math> if every vertex in <math>V - S</math> is adjacent to at least one vertex in <math>S</math>. A dominating set <math>S</math> is called a '''global dominating set''' (or '''g.d. set''') if <math>S</math> is also a dominating set of the complement <math>\bar{G}</math>.<ref name="sampathkumar1989" />

Equivalently, a dominating set <math>S</math> of <math>G</math> is a global dominating set if and only if for each vertex <math>v \in V - S</math>, there exists a vertex <math>u \in S</math> such that <math>u</math> is not adjacent to <math>v</math> in <math>G</math>.<ref name="sampathkumar1989" />

== Properties ==

The following properties hold for any graph <math>G</math>:<ref name="sampathkumar1989" />

* <math>\gamma_g(G) = \gamma_g(\bar{G})</math>
* <math>\gamma(G) \leq \gamma_g(G)</math>, where <math>\gamma(G)</math> is the [[domination number]] of <math>G</math>
* <math>\bar{\gamma}(G) \leq \gamma_g(G)</math>, where <math>\bar{\gamma}(G) = \gamma(\bar{G})</math>
* <math>\frac{\gamma(G) + \bar{\gamma}(G)}{2} \leq \gamma_g(G) \leq \gamma(G) + \bar{\gamma}(G)</math>

For a graph <math>G</math> of [[order (graph theory)|order]] <math>p</math> without isolated vertices:<ref name="sampathkumar1989" />

* <math>\gamma(G) + \gamma_g(G) \leq p + 1</math>
* <math>\gamma_g(G) \leq \max\{\chi(G), \chi(\bar{G})\}</math>, where <math>\chi(G)</math> is the [[chromatic number]] of <math>G</math>

The global domination number exhibits invariance under certain [[graph operations]]. For example, for cycles <math>C_n</math> (with <math>n \neq 3, n \neq 5</math>), the global domination number remains unchanged under the operation of edge duplication, and similarly for wheels <math>W_n</math>.<ref name="vaidya2013" />

=== Bounds ===

For a connected graph <math>G</math> of order <math>n</math> with maximum degree <math>\Delta(G)</math>, diameter <math>d(G)</math>, radius <math>r(G)</math>, and the set of [[support vertices]] (vertices adjacent to vertices with degree <math>1</math>) <math>Supp(G)</math>, the following lower bound holds:<ref name="parrainza2024" />

:<math>L = \max\left\{\frac{n}{\Delta(G)+1}, \frac{2r(G)}{3}, \frac{d(G)+1}{3}, |Supp(G)|\right\} \leq \gamma_g(G)</math>

Upper bounds have also been established:<ref name="parrainza2024" />

* <math>\gamma_g(G) \leq \min\{\Delta(G), \Delta(\bar{G})\} + 1</math>
* <math>\gamma_g(G) \leq \max\{\delta(G), \delta(\bar{G})\} + 1</math> when <math>\delta(G) = \delta(\bar{G}) > 2</math>, where <math>\delta(G)</math> is the minimum degree

== Known graphs ==

For specific families of graphs, the global domination number has been determined:<ref name="sampathkumar1989" /><ref name="vaidya2013">{{cite journal |last1=Vaidya |first1=S. K. |last2=Pandit |first2=R. M. |title=Some New Perspectives on Global Domination in Graphs |journal=ISRN Combinatorics |volume=2013 |year=2013 |pages=1–4 |doi=10.1155/2013/201654 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258390577 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

* For a [[complete graph]] <math>K_p</math> or its complement <math>\bar{K}_p</math>: <math>\gamma_g(G) = p</math>
* For a [[complete bipartite graph]] <math>K_{m,n}</math> with <math>2 \leq m \leq n</math>: <math>\gamma_g(K_{m,n}) = n</math>
* For a [[cycle graph|cycle]] <math>C_n</math> with <math>n \neq 3</math> and <math>n \neq 5</math>: <math>\gamma_g(C_n) = \lceil n/3 \rceil</math>
* For a [[path graph|path]] <math>P_n</math> with <math>n \geq 4</math>: <math>\gamma_g(P_n) = \lceil n/3 \rceil</math>
* For a [[wheel graph|wheel]] <math>W_n</math>: <math>\gamma_g(W_n) = 4</math> if <math>n = 4</math>, and <math>\gamma_g(W_n) = 3</math> otherwise

== Global domatic number ==

The '''global domatic number''' <math>d_g(G)</math> is the maximum order of a partition of the vertex set <math>V</math> into global dominating sets. Analogous to the relationship between the [[domination number]] and [[domatic number]], we have <math>d_g(G) = d_g(\bar{G})</math> and <math>d_g(G) \leq d(G) \leq \delta(G) + 1</math>, where <math>d(G)</math> is the domatic number and <math>\delta(G)</math> is the minimum degree of <math>G</math>.<ref name="sampathkumar1989" />

== Computational complexity ==

The problem of finding a minimum global dominating set is [[NP-hard]]. This was established by Brigham and Dutton (1990) through a reduction from the [[dominating set problem]], which is known to be NP-hard.<ref name="parrainza2024" /><ref name="brigham1990">{{cite journal |last1=Brigham |first1=R. C. |last2=Dutton |first2=R. D. |title=Factor domination in graphs |journal=Discrete Mathematics |volume=86 |issue=1–3 |year=1990 |pages=127–136 |doi=10.1016/0012-365X(90)90355-L |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/220190488}}</ref>

The problem remains NP-hard even for restricted graph classes, including [[planar graph]]s and [[split graph]]s. For split graphs, any global dominating set is formed either by the dominating set of the graph or by the dominating set augmented with vertices from the independent set.<ref name="parrainza2024">{{cite journal |last1=Parra Inza |first1=Ernesto |last2=Vakhania |first2=Nodari |last3=Sigarreta Almira |first3=José María |last4=Hernández Mira |first4=Frank Angel |title=Algorithms for the Global Domination Problem |journal=Computers & Operations Research |volume=172 |year=2024 |article-number=106876 |doi=10.1016/j.cor.2024.106876 |arxiv=2312.04526}}</ref>

== Algorithms ==

Both exact and heuristic algorithms have been developed for the global domination problem:<ref name="parrainza2024" />

'''Exact algorithms:'''
* An [[integer linear programming]] (ILP) formulation using <math>2n</math> constraints to ensure domination in both <math>G</math> and <math>\bar{G}</math>
* An implicit enumeration algorithm using binary search over feasible solution sizes, guided by lower and upper bounds

'''Heuristic algorithms:'''
* [[Greedy algorithm]]s that iteratively select vertices maximizing the number of newly dominated vertices in both the graph and its complement
* A purification procedure that reduces the size of a global dominating set by removing redundant vertices while maintaining the domination property

== Applications ==

Global dominating sets arise naturally in network reliability contexts. Consider a graph representing a network of roads connecting various locations, where some locations have supply stations. If the primary links (edges of <math>G</math>) may fail, maintaining supply requires that stations can reach all locations through alternative links (edges of <math>\bar{G}</math>). A global dominating set represents the minimum set of supply stations needed to maintain service regardless of which network (primary or backup) is operational.<ref name="sampathkumar1989" />

In [[social network analysis]], when modeling individuals with certain social behaviors, a standard dominating set identifies influential individuals, but does not account for potential changes in influence relationships. A global dominating set ensures coverage even if the influence network changes to its complement, providing resilience against dynamic network changes.<ref name="parrainza2024" />
